steps.name: Nervous Child
steps.text: I-I just go over there like this?

steps.name: Ill-Intentioned Citizen
steps.text: Yes. Just go over there and ask what the price is.

steps.name: Nervous Child
steps.text: A-Alright.
The child approaches the merchant's stall and timidly peruses the wares.

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: Fireworks, kid?

steps.name: Nervous Child
steps.text: Y-Yeah...

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: A special occasion? A gift? This one's real popular for celebrations!

steps.name: Nervous Child
steps.text: B-But there's a lot of dust—

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: That's normal; it's been lying in the warehouse for a while. How about this, you buy one, and I'll give you one free—

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: What's that smell—

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: Fire! It's you, isn't it?!

steps.name: Ill-Intentioned Citizen
steps.text: Hah!

steps.name: Ill-Intentioned Citizen
steps.text: What are you standing there for? Run!
The merchant tries to put out the fire to no avail, and is soon surrounded by flames himself.
The exploding fireworks draws a gawking crowd.
The 'practical joker' has long fled the scene with the child.
'But... wasn't it supposed to be a joke...'
'Serves him right for marrying a devil woman, the bastard.'
The fire's getting bigger! I'll grab the man; you get the crowd out of here!

steps.name: Defense Force Patrol
steps.text: Yes, ma'am!
The piledriver spear rips the flames apart. The sounds of explosions and crackling fire sing joyfully in cacophony.
A Vouivre emerges from the flames, spear in one hand, the merchant in the other. She puts the merchant down in a safe place, then sits beside him, wiping the soot off her face.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Ach, sorry aboot yer stall, I think I might've...

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: It's fine, fine, don't worry.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Fine? This is... fine?
She points towards the raging fire, with fireworks still leaping out from time to time.
The gawking crowd continues to grow. A drunkard, seemingly oblivious to what is going on, pulls over an unsuspecting passerby and starts dancing.
Under the setting sun is pandemonium, drunken singing mixed with angry yelling mixed with the cackle of fireworks.
This street has not been so lively since the Sarkaz took over.
It is the very picture of chaos, but the merchant, who has already calmed down, begins to laugh.

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: I haven't seen the folks so happy in a very long time. Brings back memories...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: But... it's your stall that's on fire.

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: You know what? I'm in a good mood today. Let's just call it a fireworks show for everyone!

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: Between you and me, ma'am... my wife can finally leave the city, tonight.

steps.name: Defense Force Patrol
steps.text: No injuries, ma'am. Should we go after the troublemaker?

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: Well, nobody got hurt—

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: We've got a duty to handle anyone who commits an offense.

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: Well, thank you, in any case. Say, can you dance? Or play an instrument?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: Can't let good fireworks go to waste, can I?

steps.name: Amiable Merchant
steps.text: Maybe my wife will hear the commotion. My way of saying goodbye.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: *sigh* I'm startin' to miss wartime. Even workin' on the farm. Anythin's easier than this 'keepin' the peace' business.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: But, hey, if everyone's happy, who'm I tae complain?
Once she is satisfied that there is no danger, she lies down on a crate by the roadside, stretches, and lets the beams of the setting sun fall upon her face.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Gimme a haystack over this any day.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Where are you, Chenchen...?

steps.name: Nervous Child
steps.text: Wh-Why did you burn his stall? You said you were just going to snitch something!

steps.name: Ill-Intentioned Citizen
steps.text: That shameless bastard's own fault for marrying a devil.

steps.name: Ill-Intentioned Citizen
steps.text: On the bright side, maybe somebody's already lynched his wife—

steps.name: Ill-Intentioned Citizen
steps.text: Whoa!

steps.name: Ill-Intentioned Citizen
steps.text: Who the feck are you?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Now's your chance to run, kid.

steps.name: Nervous Child
steps.text: O-Okay!

steps.name: Ill-Intentioned Citizen
steps.text: Wh-What do you want?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Just doing a favor for a client. Maybe it'll bring in future business.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: What's the situation with this batch?

steps.name: Tired Mercenary
steps.text: Coast is clear, and the head count checks out, no problem. But word on the streets is that Parliament is looking for you.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Nothing they can actually do about it. Same as before, don't cause any trouble.

steps.name: Tired Mercenary
steps.text: Speaking of trouble...

steps.name: Tired Mercenary
steps.text: There's a kid in this batch that's giving us a hard time.

steps.name: Indignant Child
steps.text: Why can't I see my dad one last time before we leave?

steps.name: Indignant Child
steps.text: This man says there's fireworks outside. It's dad's fireworks!

steps.name: Nervous Woman
steps.text: Shh, quiet.

steps.name: Indignant Child
steps.text: You don't want to leave either, do you, Mum—
The Sarkaz covers the child's mouth and holds her tightly, gazing up nervously at the woman looking quietly down at her.

steps.name: Nervous Woman
steps.text: I'm sorry, she's just not used to this... her father never left her side, even during the war.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Our deal with your husband was to get you out of the city. The rest is not my business.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: If you want to stay, that's also your own decision.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Ma'am, they're just scared because they've never been through anything like this.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: None of us have... Don't worry, I'll take care of the girl. She won't cause you any trouble.

steps.name: Indignant Child
steps.text: But where are we going? What about Dad?

steps.name: Nervous Woman
steps.text: He'll come find us once he's taken care of things at home.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: *sigh* I knew this day would come, the day the people from Kazdel came.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: You don't like the Military Commission? Isn't Theresis your legendary hero?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I'm every bit the Londinier that you are. I've never been anywhere else since I was born, and I don't know no Theresis.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Your accent, that's not how commoners talk. I take it you ended up here because of the folks from Kazdel?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Never mind.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: You're a good person, ma'am. No one else would come close to us at a time like this.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Without you, the new Parliament might've... nothing to be surprised, I suppose. The bigwigs never change, whatever happens.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I've seen enough in my lifetime.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: This new Parliament is different—

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Maybe. For people like us, though, it all feels the same.
The aged Sarkaz soothes the sobbing child and sighs.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Don't be afraid, child. Your father is an honest man, more honest than most people I've met. He'll find you.

steps.name: Indignant Child
steps.text: Alright... but where will you go after leaving here?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I plan on visiting some old friends. They left during the withdrawal with their twins, who work for a pharmaceutical company.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Do you know them, ma'am?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: No. We have no time. You should get ready to leave.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: What is your name, ma'am?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: We will not meet again.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Humor an old woman, won't you? I just want to thank you, on behalf of myself, and all those who are afraid of you—

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: And I would rather not direct this gratitude to a code name that's ready to be cast aside any time.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Allerdale.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Beautiful name. Thank you, Allerdale.
Allerdale. A name that should have been laid to rest in the Mausoleum of Kings.

In the darkness where even the passage of time became blurred, she had sought to die in the ruins of history, to be forgotten by all those whom she disappointed, yet she was afraid to die, afraid to be forgotten.
But when muddy water dripped from the hole that the Steam Knight left behind and fell upon her palm, she opened her eyes and saw light.
What lay at the end of the light was life, and submission again.
Her hesitation may have lasted three days, or three minutes... in the end, she made the same choice as she once did.
She recited it over and over in her mind, and crawled quietly into the light.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: What do you mean, the reservation with Madam Major is no longer valid and I have to get in queue again?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Should we be trying to buy time for the Infected who can't get medication?

steps.name: Unperturbed Official
steps.text: I'm afraid the reservation system is under maintenance. There are a lot of files that need to be organized following Madam Major's passing.

steps.name: Unperturbed Official
steps.text: However, we are all very busy with preparations for Madam Major's funeral.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: How long are we talking?

steps.name: Unperturbed Official
steps.text: It should be up and running within seven business days. We will inform you as soon as reasonably possible.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Have you been to the Center for Biological Infection Control? More and more citizens whose conditions are deteriorating rapidly are being sent there by the day.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Most Londiniers didn't know how to handle acute Oripathy attacks before the war. The ones who need help the most are the ones getting the least of it.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: They can't afford to wait... not to mention the proliferation of drugs that have little actual effectiveness...

steps.name: Unperturbed Official
steps.text: Your feedback is noted. We will pass it on to the Center for Biological Infection Control. Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Tell me where the Speaker's office is.

steps.name: Unperturbed Official
steps.text: If you would like to visit the Speaker, I can assist you in making a reservation—

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: No need to ask him. I know where the Speaker is.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Come with me, Eliseo.

steps.name: Unperturbed Official
steps.text: I apologize for the inconvenience. Please let us know if you need any other assistance. And thank you for the coffee, sir.

steps.name: Unperturbed Official
steps.text: It is a very valuable gift.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Aren't you furious, Diane? This is no way for them to behave. I came to Londinium to—

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: To save us?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: No... that's not what I mean.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: But it's what you think, isn't it?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I-I mean no offense. I'm grateful that you've put a roof over my head, but I also see there's nothing but chaos in the matter of helping the Infected here.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I get that it takes time to build up and improve systems and workflows. Please understand, though, that it was my job to raise such issues, back in Columbia.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I just want to see more regulated and effective workflow to provide help to more Infected. And if I may say so, we're a little ahead on that front.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I've never been to Columbia, Eliseo, and I don't know how people like us are treated back where you call home.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I would love to see it, if I get the chance.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: But that gentleman has done nothing wrong. He has done what was tasked of him in such cases; in fact, he has done it better than any of his predecessors.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Londinium has many problems. But things are getting better, even better than before the war.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: It seems you trust this new Parliament?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: No, but I trust the Speaker. Come, I'll take you to her.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: How do you know where she is?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I take it you Columbians are not in the habit of listening to the broadcasts.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Well, we're more used to watching...

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Never mind. Where is the Speaker?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: At the memorial service for Madam Major.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Here? There are so many people, how do we get to the Speaker?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Come with me. I know a shortcut.
Through the window, Eliseo sees Vina Victoria for the first time.
He has done his homework, and heard the legends of the young Speaker during the war.
He thought the Speaker would be more impressive.
When he sees the well-dressed Aslan speaking at the podium, he feels nothing but disappointment—
Vina Victoria is not nearly as splendid as he imagined.
Are you lost?
If you're here for the service, the entrance is that way.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Would you like a hand, Eliseo?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Oh, er, thank you.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Hey, how did you—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I was the one who put the files on Pure Heart Medical—and yourself—on the Speaker's table, long before you arrived in Londinium.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: So you know what I'm here for?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: And the Speaker knows what I've been trying to do for the past few days?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Unfortunately, it's not that simple.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I thought the Speaker would be different from the other nobles I've met.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Eliseo!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It's fine. I would just like to clear up the misunderstanding. This is not Columbia, Eliseo, and it is arrogance to judge us by your standards.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Sometimes, we must follow the rules first, in order to change things.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Not even she could do it?
Inside the hall, Vina is muttering something with a sad expression on her face, but they cannot hear what she is saying.
Delphine meets Diane's gaze, then quickly averts her eyes.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Was Madam Major another victim of the rules?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: No, only a respectable woman. One of those 'nobles' you were talking about.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: She could have stayed in Normandy, far from danger, but she came of her own accord to the chaos of Londinium in order to help the people here.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: She refused to stop working, even as her condition deteriorated, trying to help as many people as she could. Just like you, Eliseo.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Our conflict with her was only because of the harm that her radicalness and stubbornness were doing to herself.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: There are no dark secrets, no conspiracies behind her passing. She was not a 'victim'.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I'm sorry, I... I didn't know.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: But that makes it even harder to understand. Why do you refuse to work with Pure Heart? We're just trying to solve your problems.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Are you aware that Pure Heart Medical is backed by the Columbian Department of Defense and the Maylander Foundation?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Of course. The military and the Foundation have always been our main stakeholders.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You... are a good, responsible man. Feel free to come and find me, if you insist on carrying out that responsibility.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Oh, er... you are...?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Delphine Windermere. You may call me Delphine. Looks like your company has work to do when it comes to client research.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I'm not giving up, Lady Delphine. I believe we can help with Londinium.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I can't make any promises on behalf of Vina or Parliament. But believe me when I say that we want to heal this city more than anyone else.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But, if you would like, you can come with me, to say goodbye to Madam Major...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: And to all those who have died in the chaos of the past few years.
The bell of mourning tolls. Fowlbeasts glide close to the ground, a sign of impeding rain.
Right now, though, nobody pays any heed. Their heads are bowed.
No tears are shed. War has already spent the city of its last drop.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: All leads point to this place being Millscar's hideout. Why are you still taking your time?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Don't you think it's too easy?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Besides, there has been rumors of unidentified Sarkaz activity here. Can't hurt to be careful.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I say it can't hurt to have an accident or two. Good exercise.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Why do you think I refused to help Morgan with her stupid paperwork?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: You're an upright girl, to come along like this. I thought you'd shut yourself up in the tower as soon as you came back.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: You really ought to be staying put at the ship, Hannah. How many times has Medical reminded you about your condition—

spans.text: really ought to be staying put at the ship, Hannah. How many times has Medical reminded you about your condition—

steps.text: The sound of bells echoes in the sky above the city. As if everything has gone quiet for a moment.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: The memorial service has started.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Well—no time to wallow in sentiment. Let's go, Dagda. I don't want to get my arse kicked while I'm trying to wipe the tears from my eyes.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Sometimes I just don't know what to do with you, Hannah.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: What do we do if we run into Allerdale?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Punch her in the gut and leave the rest for Vina to worry about.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Who's there?!
I'm afraid you won't find her. It's not you she wants to see.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Who are you?!
The Rose Riverside's Canoe.
